transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Sana (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO, Marigold), Rajesh (Platform), Marta (Security), Tommy (SRE)

Summary:
00:00 Intro and purpose - Marigold is planning to decommission their OpenAI-hosted endpoints and evaluate options (hosted Redwood, dedicated pool, or private VPC) while keeping parity with current evals and preserving data residency and KMS controls. They want a low-risk exit path with a 6-8 week pilot and a production cutover plan.

Topics covered:
- Compatibility with vLLM/TGI stack and model artifact formats (LLM checkpoints, tokenizer differences)
- Eval parity: deterministic prompts vs sampling and canary metrics
- Operational concerns: KV cache warmup, prefix caching, burst capacity, autoscaling and throttling
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs and retention, data residency EU requirement
- Migration runbook: cutover, rollback, shadow testing, metrics to monitor

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed, occasional errors)

[00:00] Evan Rivera: Hey thanks everyone for joining. Quick intro, I'm Evan, AE for Redwood Inference, and Sana here is our solutions engineer who will own the technical runbook.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hi all, I'm Lena, CTO at Marigold, we run conversational search and checkout assistants for retailers. We're looking at decommissioning our OpenAI endpoints — costs are spiking and we need more control over data.
[00:20] Rajesh Menon: Yeah, and we have some components on Azure already, also trialed Anthropic for safety — but mostly it's vLLM on our side for dev tests and TGI for some newer models. We need to know how far Redwood will match our token accounting and eval scores.
[00:35] Sana Gupta: Totally, that's a common concern. Quick question — on your vLLM/TGI side are you using custom kernels or stock releases? Is quantization applied?
[00:42] Rajesh Menon: We have a mix, some Q4_0 quantized ints for prod and float16 for dev. Also some local kernels patched for our latency targets — so mapping is important.
[00:55] [crosstalk] Evan Rivera: Right, so our dedicated runtime supports a range of quant formats and we do kernel selection at compile time — but it's helpful to capture examples. Sana, can you talk through how we test parity?
[01:05] Sana Gupta: Sure — we usually start with a determinis.. determinis- (laughs) deterministic prompt set plus a sampling set. Two things: eval parity (quality) where we compare metrics like exact match, helpfulness, hallucination rate, and then perf parity where we run token-per-second and p95 latency tests under simulated traffic. For model mapping we create a compatibility matrix: model name, weights format, tokenizer id, quant profile, expected memory.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: Important: we can't have any European PII cross-border, so private deployment or EU-hosted dedicated pools are a must. Our legal team requires KMS integration and audit logs for 12 months.
[01:42] Marta Silva: And on top we need SSO for the console, RBAC to restrict who can pull model artifacts, and HSM-backed keys. Also need an encryption-in-transit proof point for private deployment.
[01:55] Sana Gupta: We support customer-managed KMS and HSM for Private; Dedicated can be configured for isolated tenancy with KMS integration as well. For hosted, tokenization/data retention policies can be adjusted, but if PII policies are strict you usually go Dedicated or Private.
[02:12] Rajesh Menon: How do you handle model fallbacks? Right now we have an OpenAI-based routing that downgrades to a cheaper model on spikes and retries.
[02:20] Evan Rivera: We provide smart routing—policy rules let you route by cost, latency or model version. You can set automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant or to a cloud-region fallback. During a rollout we recommend canary traffic and automated rollback triggers.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: For cutover, we want a shadowing period of 2 weeks then progressive ramp. Also need a checklist for decommissioning existing keys and webhooks.
[02:47] Sana Gupta: We'll include a step-by-step runbook: shadow mode -> perf benchmarks -> canary -> full cutover. We'll instrument metrics to look at latency p50/p95, token cost delta, regression alerts based on your prompt test set.
[03:00] [15:00 summary jump — meeting continues deep dive]
[15:12] Sana Gupta: Quick note on KV cache — your current vLLM setup uses a custom cache TTL of 30s. Our runtime supports prefix and KV caching; sometimes cache semantics differ which changes warmup behavior. We can emulate your TTLs during the pilot to get realistic latency curves.
[15:35] Rajesh Menon: That's a big one. We saw cold starts spike to 750ms p95 during holiday loads — need to know batching behavior and how Redwood's continuous batching affects 90%ile.
[15:48] Sana Gupta: We do continuous batching with latency SLO knobs. You can cap batch sizes or favor single-request low latency classes. We'll capture your traffic mix and recommend optimal batching settings.
[16:05] Lena Ortiz: Eval parity — how repeatable are answers? We rely on certain deterministic completions for admin flows. If Redwood's runtime adds small tokenization diffs we need to account for that.
[16:20] Evan Rivera: On tokenization we can run a side-by-side diff of token ids across model artifacts. For deterministic flows we recommend pinning model versions and seed settings; for sampling flows we'll run A/B tests to monitor drift.
[16:34] Marta Silva: Security — can you generate per-request audit logs and include user id, model version, and checksum of prompt? We need an immutability guarantee for 12 months.
[16:45] Sana Gupta: Yes, audit logs are available; for Private we can ship logs to your S3/GCS in encrypted form, and we support append-only storage patterns for compliance. We'll provide retention controls.
[17:00] [side comment] Tommy Li: Are there any known incompatibilities with TGI? We use TGI for some prompt templating and it expects certain weight layouts.
[17:12] Sana Gupta: We have a TGI compatibility layer in our onboarding playbook — most TGI models map fine but there are edge cases with custom operators. We'll want a sample model and we'll run a conversion check.
[17:28] Rajesh Menon: Performance numbers — can you share sample p95 / tps for a baseline Llama-2-13b quantized run on dedicated 8xA40 pool?
[17:37] Evan Rivera: We'll share benchmark references in the deck, and for your exact traffic we'll run targeted tests during the pilot. Expect dedicated pools to have predictable throughput; hosted may have slightly higher variance but faster time-to-value.
[17:50] Lena Ortiz: Ok cost — we need clear per-token comparisons and a model mapping table, also any egress or regional fees for EU.
[18:00] Evan Rivera: We'll send a pricing matrix and example cost model based on your token histogram you share. Also include burst pricing for holiday peaks and reserved commit options for Dedicated.
[18:15] [mis-transcribed] Speaker 2: can you — sorry, just to confirm will Redwood support our internal policy automation?
[18:20] Sana Gupta: Yes, we can integrate with your policy engine via webhooks and pre-/post-process hooks. For sensitive flows we can redact tokens at ingestion if needed.
[18:35] [closing 55:00 mark summary and next steps]
[55:10] Evan Rivera: Recap — we'll deliver pricing + SOW, benchmark runbook, and security docs. Marigold will share prompts and traffic profile. Next call we'll be technical deep-dive with the infra team to schedule the pilot.
[55:35] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. I want the SRE and legal looped in on the docs. Thanks everyone.
[55:45] Marta Silva: Thanks.
